subject: Critical: FjordRetail streaming integration errors — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Lena Håkansson <lena@fjordretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@fjordretail.com>, Fjord Retail Platform Team <platform@fjordretail.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 21:03:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failures & timeouts during tonight's peak (logs attached)

Marissa,

We're seeing a serious regression in checkout throughput starting ~20:45 PDT tonight. Approximately 7% of POST /generate/stream requests are returning truncated streaming responses or hanging until our client times out. This started after we rolled a small proxy change; we've temporarily rolled it back but the errors continued for several minutes afterward.

Symptoms:
- p99 latency up to 12s (typical ~300ms)
- 502/504 for chunked streaming endpoints, plus client-level parse exceptions in our frontend SDK
- Customers report carts being lost when streams fail mid-token

Attached: fjord_err_20260928.log (snippet of client-side stack traces) and a short PCAP showing a suspected split-header sequence.

We need immediate help diagnosing whether this is a Redwood runtime regression or an integration edge-case triggered by our proxy rewrite. Can you escalate on your side? We have a scheduled renewal review next week and this is high-impact.

—Lena
Lena Håkansson
Head of Platform Engineering, Fjord Retail

Attachment: fjord_err_20260928.log (text), pcap_segment_20260928.pcap (pcap)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Håkansson <lena@fjordretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 22:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures & timeouts during tonight's peak (logs attached)

Lena — thanks for the quick report and attachments. We're on this.

Preliminary triage notes:
- I kicked off a correlated query across ingress logs and we're seeing an uptick in 50x responses from our streaming gateway exactly in the window you called out.
- The PCAP you sent shows multiple TCP frames where the streaming headers appear split across packets; historically we've seen certain client-side proxies (and older SDKs) treat those sequences differently.

Immediate actions:
1) Sean, please reproduce against a local harness with a proxy that inserts split header frames (I can share the PCAP).
2) Neha, can your team look for any recent changes to the dechunker/streaming parser that might be sensitive to header fragmentation?
3) Lena, can you confirm whether the proxy change altered header coalescing or introduced any ALPN/HTTP2 intermediaries?

We'll provide hourly updates until we have a root cause. If this ends up being a parsing edge-case on our SDK/runtime, we will propose a mitigation (server-side tolerant-mode + patch rollout).

Marissa Cole
Principal Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Fjord Retail Platform Team <platform@fjordretail.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Checkout failures & timeouts during tonight's peak (logs attached)

Marissa / Sean — quick engineering update after an overnight dive.

What we did:
- Replayed the PCAP into a local harness that mirrors our streaming gateway behavior (HTTP/2, chunked responses).
- Instrumented the streaming dechunker and saw that when the initial header block is split across two frames with an intermediate 1-3 byte payload, our parser's header-assembly heuristic occasionally discards the intermediary boundary marker and treats the remainder as body bytes. That results in a malformed header sequence delivered to the client, causing client SDK parse exceptions and the 502/504s reported.

Root cause hypothesis:
- A recent micro-optimization in the dechunker (PR#4721) changed the assembly order for header segments when they are not aligned to frame boundaries. Under low-volume conditions this wasn't triggered, but with Fjord's proxy behavior + peak concurrency we can reproduce reliably.

Short-term mitigations (we can ship within hours):
- Roll back the assembly heuristic in the dechunker (will require a canary to prod): patch ready.
- Add server-side tolerant-mode: if header assembly fails, respond with a 503 and a diagnostic header (X-RW-DIAG) so downstream SDKs can surface clearer errors instead of silent parse failures.

Longer-term:
- Add fuzz tests for split-header sequences and include a PCAP-based regression harness in CI.

I'm preparing a patch and rolling it to our staging canary now. ETA for canary rollout: 2 hours. Full prod rollback/patch if canary looks good: 4–6 hours.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Engineering Manager, Runtime
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Critical: FjordRetail streaming integration errors — exec attention requested

Rishi — looping you in because Fjord is a top-tier renewal next week (DEAL-2026-FJORD-03). Engineering has a reproducible root cause: the dechunker optimization (PR#4721) mishandles split header frames when a proxy inserts byte-level splits. Neha has a rollback + patch that can be canaried within ~2 hours and fully rolled in 4–6 hours pending canary results.

Why this needs exec attention now:
- Business impact: Fjord is experiencing aborted checkouts and p99 latency spikes during peak traffic, which directly affects revenue and the upcoming renewal conversation.
- Customer escalation: Lena requested executive visibility in her original note.
- Mitigation coordination: we should pre-approve an emergency prod patch (patch is low-risk but touches the runtime parsing path).

Proposed ask:
1) Rishi — approval for an emergency canary + rollback/patch path and priority on the rollout window.
2) I will coordinate communications with Fjord (we propose a mitigation note + postmortem follow-up).
3) Ops — prepare monitoring hooks to immediately revert if any regression appears.

Attached are the log snippet and PCAP from Fjord for your review. I'll be on the bridge for the canary at 10:30 PDT with Sean & Neha.

Thanks,
Marissa
Principal Account Lead, Redwood Inference
